title: Stop Shipping Maven Into Production (Multi-Stage Docker)
description:
Most Java Dockerfiles accidentally ship the entire Maven build toolchain into production. This Short shows the two-stage fix: compile in a throwaway Maven/JDK stage, then copy just the finished jar into a slim JRE image running as a non-root user. Same app, a fraction of the image size, way less attack surface.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/07-containerization-deployment/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Here's a Docker mistake almost every Java developer makes: shipping the entire Maven toolchain straight into production.
The build stage compiles with a full Maven and JDK image -- fine, because this bulky stage never actually ships.

display.code:
# ---- Build stage ----
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21 AS build
WORKDIR /app

COPY pom.xml .
RUN mvn dependency:go-offline -B

COPY src ./src
RUN mvn package -DskipTests -B

beats.narration: A second stage starts completely fresh: just a slim JRE Alpine image, and it copies in only the finished jar file.

display.code:
# ---- Runtime stage ----
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
WORKDIR /app

RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
USER app

COPY --from=build /app/target/order-service-*.jar app.jar

EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

beats.narration: One command builds the image, another runs it and maps the port -- no build tools, no dependency drama, no 'works on my machine.'

display.code:
docker build -t order-service:latest .

docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -e DB_PASSWORD='SuperSecret123!' \
  order-service:latest

beats.narration: That's a multi-stage Dockerfile in about twenty lines, and it cuts your production image down to a fraction of the size. Full breakdown's linked below.
